changes: p3: name given as best reading 'Taruṇaprabha' instead of the non-name 'Taranijaprabha'; confidence lowered to low (corrupt form; 'Jinaprabha' is also possible)
p1: 'naraveśasarasvatī' kept in titles but flagged in notes as an honorific epithet ('Sarasvatī in human guise'), not an office
notes: added that all persons belong to the composition of the commentary, not to this copy, and that the catalogue title 'Śiṣuhitaiṣiṇī' should read Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī

notes: This is a chapter colophon inside the text, at the end of sarga 15 of Cāritravardhana's Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī commentary on the Raghuvaṃśa ('rāghavīyaṭīkā'). The catalogue spells the title 'Śiṣuhitaiṣiṇī' and the colophon has 'śuṣuhitaiṣiṇyāṃ'; both stand for Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī. It gives no scribe, date or place for this copy. Everyone named here belongs to the composition of the commentary, not to this copy. Araḍakamalla, of the Śrīmāla lineage, asked for the commentary to be written ('sabhyārthita', probably meant as 'abhyarthita'), so he is the patron of the original work. 'taranija(4)prābhācārya' is corrupt. Possible readings are Taruṇaprabhācārya or (kharatara-gacchīya-)Jinaprabhācārya. Other sources give Cāritravardhana's teacher as Kalyāṇarāja, which this colophon does not confirm. 'prapādapadmopajīvi' probably stands for '-pada-padmopajīvi' (living at the lotus feet of). 'naraveśasarasvatī' is probably an epithet meaning 'Sarasvatī in human form' ('naraveṣa-'), not an office.
